cases.architecture: Payload CMS 3 application in TypeScript: collection configs with their own `endpoints` arrays plus root endpoints, all assembled in src/payload.config.ts; Payload's Local API over MongoDB (@payloadcms/db-mongodb) is the only data layer; the caller's identity is `req.user`, populated by the `users` auth collection and carrying a role and a tenant relationship.
cases.why: The `:id` route parameter is handed to `payload.findByID` with `overrideAccess: true`, which switches off the very `access.read` filter the comment above it relies on, so any authenticated caller — a buyer in another organisation, or an external supplier user — can read any purchase order's reference, status, supplier and approval trail by guessing or replaying an id.

cases.why: Same untrusted `:id` and the same `overrideAccess: true` read, but the id is only one clause of a `where` whose other clause is `ownershipClause(user)`, pinning the query to the caller's `tenant` (or `supplierCode` for supplier users), so another organisation's invoice id matches nothing and the handler answers 404. `ownershipClause` throws rather than returning an empty clause when ownership cannot be established.

cases.why: `access.read` on the payout-accounts collection returns `true` unconditionally, so the collection's own REST and GraphQL surface hands the IBAN, BIC, mandate reference and SEPA creditor id of every organisation to any caller, including an unauthenticated one. The comment assumes the admin panel's login is the gate, but the collection API is reachable without it.

cases.why: The shared access helpers deny anonymous callers outright and otherwise return a `Where` that pins every read and write to the caller's own tenant; the only `return true` in them is reached solely on the `platform-admin` role, so the truthy return is a role decision rather than an open collection.

cases.why: The PATCH /me/profile handler spreads the entire request body into `payload.update` with `overrideAccess: true`, and `overrideAccess` skips field-level access control as well as collection access, so a caller can include `role: 'platform-admin'`, another `tenant` id or a `supplierCode` in the body and rewrite their own privileges — the field-level `access.update` guards the comment relies on never run.

cases.why: The same `payload.update` with `overrideAccess: true` on a body-derived object, but the data is assembled by copying only the four names in `EDITABLE_BILLING_FIELDS` and validating each one, so `apiCredentials`, `payoutAccount`, `slug` and `suspendedAt` in the body are never read; the target id is also compared against the caller's own tenant before the write.

cases.why: `body.reference` is dropped into the `where` clause as the whole field condition instead of as the value of an operator, so posting `{"reference": {"not_equals": "__none__"}}` turns the `overrideAccess: true` find into a dump of up to twenty arbitrary purchase orders — references, statuses, supplier names and delivery dates from every organisation — on an endpoint that has no session at all.

import path from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

import { mongooseAdapter } from '@payloadcms/db-mongodb'
import { lexicalEditor } from '@payloadcms/richtext-lexical'
import { buildConfig } from 'payload'

import { Invoices } from './collections/Invoices'
import { PayoutAccounts } from './collections/PayoutAccounts'
import { PurchaseOrders } from './collections/PurchaseOrders'
import { Tenants } from './collections/Tenants'
import { Users } from './collections/Users'
import { attachmentDownloadEndpoint } from './endpoints/attachment-download'
import { invoiceReferenceLookupEndpoint } from './endpoints/invoice-reference-lookup'
import { invoiceStatementEndpoint } from './endpoints/invoice-statements'
import { orderFeedEndpoint } from './endpoints/order-feed'
import { orderTrackingEndpoint } from './endpoints/order-tracking'
import { reportExportEndpoint } from './endpoints/report-export'

const dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))

const serverURL = process.env.PAYLOAD_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'

const payloadSecret = process.env.PAYLOAD_SECRET
if (!payloadSecret) {
  throw new Error('PAYLOAD_SECRET is required. Copy .env.example and fill it in before booting.')
}

export default buildConfig({
  serverURL,
  routes: {
    // Root-level endpoints below are served under this prefix, so
    // `path: '/order-feed'` answers on GET /api/order-feed.
    api: '/api',
    admin: '/admin',
  },
  admin: {
    user: Users.slug,
    importMap: { baseDir: path.resolve(dirname) },
    meta: { titleSuffix: ' — Orderbook' },
  },
  collections: [Users, Tenants, PurchaseOrders, Invoices, PayoutAccounts],
  endpoints: [
    orderTrackingEndpoint,
    invoiceReferenceLookupEndpoint,
    invoiceStatementEndpoint,
    orderFeedEndpoint,
    attachmentDownloadEndpoint,
    reportExportEndpoint,
  ],
  editor: lexicalEditor(),
  secret: payloadSecret,
  typescript: { outputFile: path.resolve(dirname, 'payload-types.ts') },
  db: mongooseAdapter({
    // Local development database; staging and production come from the env.
    url: process.env.DATABASE_URI ?? 'mongodb://orderbook:orderbook@localhost:27017/orderbook',
  }),
  cors: [serverURL],
  csrf: [serverURL],
  graphQL: { disable: false },
  telemetry: false,
})
